title: The Mean of a Geometric Distribution and Expected Waiting Times

questions.title: Expected Value of a Geometric Distribution

parts.text: The random variable $X$ has a geometric distribution with success parameter $p = 0.05$. Find $E(X)$, and interpret this value in words.

questions.title: Recovering Success Probability from the Geometric Mean

parts.text: The expected number of trials required to achieve the first success in a geometric distribution is $16$. Find the exact probability of success $p$ on each independent trial.

questions.title: Expected Number of Throws for a Dice Total of 9

parts.text: Two fair six-sided dice are thrown repeatedly until their total score is 9. Let $X$ be the number of throws required. Find $E(X)$.

questions.title: Probability of Exceeding a Non-Integer Geometric Mean

parts.text: The random variable $X$ has a geometric distribution with $p = 0.40$. Find $E(X)$, and calculate $P(X > E(X))$.

questions.title: Fractional Mean and Long-Run Average Interpretation

parts.text: A spinner has 8 equal sectors, of which 3 are shaded. The spinner is spun repeatedly until it lands on a shaded sector. Let $X$ be the number of spins required. Find $E(X)$ as an exact fraction, and state why $E(X)$ is not a possible value of $X$.

questions.title: Expectation of a Linear Cost Function

parts.text: A machine is tested repeatedly until a fault is detected, where the probability of a fault on any trial is $p = 0.25$. The cost in dollars of the testing process is given by $C = 15 + 5X$, where $X$ is the number of trials required. Find $E(C)$.

questions.title: Driving Certification: Expected Attempts and Early Passing

parts.text: A candidate takes a practical driving test repeatedly until passing. The candidate passes on any attempt with probability $0.24$, independently of previous attempts. Let $X$ be the number of attempts required. Find $E(X)$ as an exact fraction in simplest form, and explain what this value represents.
Find the probability that the candidate passes the test on fewer than 3 attempts, giving your answer as an exact decimal.

questions.title: Spin Machine Mean Parameter and Tail Analysis

parts.text: A game is played repeatedly until a jackpot is hit. Let $X$ be the number of plays required, where $X \sim \text{Geo}(p)$. Given that the expected number of plays is $E(X) = 12.5$, find the exact value of $p$.
Using $p = 0.08$, find $P(X = 5)$ and $P(X > 8)$, giving both answers correct to 4 significant figures.

questions.title: Carnival Game: Linear Profit Transformation and Positive Gain

parts.text: A contestant plays a game repeatedly until winning a prize. The probability of winning on each turn is $p = 0.16$, independently of other turns. Let $X$ be the number of turns required. Find $E(X)$.

Each turn costs $\$10$, and winning the prize awards a fixed cash payout of $\$100$. The contestant's net profit in dollars is given by $G = 100 - 10X$. Find $E(G)$, and find the probability that the contestant makes a strictly positive net profit ($G > 0$), giving your answer correct to 4 significant figures.

questions.title: Probability of Exceeding the Mean: Integer vs Non-Integer Cases

parts.text: The random variable $X$ has a geometric distribution with $p = 0.20$. Find $E(X)$, and calculate $P(X > E(X))$, giving your answer as an exact decimal.
The random variable $Y$ has a geometric distribution with $p = 0.35$. Find $E(Y)$, and calculate $P(Y > E(Y))$, giving your answer as an exact decimal.

questions.title: Machine Comparison: Mean Separation and Quality Threshold

parts.text: Two machines, $A$ and $B$, produce identical parts independently. Machine $A$ produces defective parts with probability $0.05$, and Machine $B$ produces defective parts with probability $0.08$. Parts from each machine are tested until the first defective part is found. Let $X_A$ and $X_B$ be the number of parts tested from Machine $A$ and Machine $B$ respectively. Find $E(X_A)$, $E(X_B)$, and $E(X_A - X_B)$.
Find $P(X_B > 15)$, and find the least number of parts $n$ that must be tested from Machine $B$ such that the probability of finding at least one defective part is greater than $0.85$.

questions.title: Double Six Waiting Time: Long-Run Mean to Multi-Player Contest

parts.text: A player throws two fair six-sided dice repeatedly until a double 6 is obtained. Let $X$ be the number of throws required. Find $E(X)$, and find $P(X = 36)$, giving the probability correct to 4 significant figures.
Find the probability that the number of throws required exceeds the expected number of throws ($P(X > E(X))$), giving your answer correct to 4 significant figures.

Four players independently throw their own pair of fair dice until obtaining their first double 6. Find the probability that at least 2 of the 4 players need more than the expected number of throws (more than 36 throws), giving your answer correct to 3 significant figures.

questions.title: Exploratory Resource Drilling: Expected Profit, Loss Risk, and Viability Threshold

parts.text: An exploration company drills exploratory wells one by one until finding a productive oil deposit. Each drill succeeds independently with probability $0.08$. Let $X$ be the number of wells drilled. Each well costs $\$2$ million to drill, and a productive deposit yields revenue of $\$40$ million. The net profit in millions of dollars is given by $V = 40 - 2X$. Find $E(X)$ and $E(V)$.
Find the probability that the company makes a net financial loss on the operation ($V < 0$), giving your answer correct to 4 significant figures.

The company has an initial operational budget covering up to 15 wells. If no productive well is found within 15 wells, the project is abandoned. Find the probability that the project is abandoned, and find the least number of wells $M$ that would ensure the probability of finding at least one productive well is at least $0.90$.
